key_fit: 阿=a ok (影, vowel onset); 利=ri/li ok (來; r/l ambiguous); 尼=ni ok (孃 ɳ-, 脂: ni/nī; key ni, ne, ṇī)
attestation: Ārhan/Arhang, the Oxus ford of the Arabic itineraries (Iṣṭakhrī; Marquart, Minorsky), reported by Ji
quote: 馬迦特將阿利尼比定爲Ärhan 或Arhang,並
site_lead: Arhan/Arhang ford near Hazrat Imam (Ḥudūd al-ʿĀlam comm.: 'From the Arhan ford (B) to Halavard 2 marhalas'; Minorsky: near, not at, Hazrat-Imam)
note: The characters give a-ri-ni (or a-li-ni). The attested place name Arhan/Arhang fits only a-r-: there is no character for the h (曉/匣 would be needed, e.g. 曷/喝), and 尼 gives -ni, not -han/-haṅ. So the name equation Arhan = 阿利尼 is loose; the identification rests on the ford and the Oxus-bank description (帶縛蒭河兩岸) more than on the name. *arini preferred to *alini only because of Arhan. Library search not useful (Iranian name). Three short open syllables: chance matches easy.

key_fit: 訖=k ok (見 + -t, closed C1 before r; key k ×2, 訖利 krī); 栗=ṛ ok (來 + -t; key ṛ ×3); 瑟=ṣ ok (生 + -t, closed C1 before m); 摩=ma ok

quote: Kišm wird bei Hiian-čuang (I 28. II 196. Hoei-li 269) unter der sanskritisierten
site_lead: Kishm (Kišm) on the Kokcha between Taliqan and Faizabad (Ḥudūd comm. p. 331; Ji)
note: The characters render kṛṣma exactly by the key (stop+r cluster with 訖栗 as in 姞栗 gṛ; ṣ-cluster with 瑟). Kišm has no r: either XZ heard an older *Kiršm/*Kṛšm or he Sanskritised the name (Marquart). š rendered by 生 (ṣ) as for Iranian š elsewhere (鑊沙 Wakhsh). No Sanskrit attestation (library: kṛṣma only as kṛṣmāṇḍa etc.).

key_fit: 鉢=pa(r) ok (幫 p- + -t; key p, pa, par); 利=ri/r ok (來; cf. non-Indic 貨利習彌伽 Khwā-ri-zm); 曷=ghar ok for Iranian γ (匣 ɣ- + -t = -r; cf. 曷邏胡 rāgh)
attestation: Parghar (var. Parkhar, Farghar), Ḥudūd al-ʿĀlam §6.7-8 (between Badhakhshan and Parghar; the Kulab river reaches Parghar and falls into the Jayhun); village Parkhar still exists (Minorsky)
quote: flows into the Jayhun between Badhakhshan and Parghar.
site_lead: Parkhar (Farkhor), N bank of the Panj at the mouth of the Kulab river (Kchi-Surkhab), Tajikistan (Ḥudūd comm.; Barthold via Ji)
note: Parghar fits all three characters: p (幫), r (利, as 利 for the r of Khwārizm), γar (匣 ɣ- with -t for r). Farkhar (S of the Oxus, SE of Taliqan) fits less well: kh would be 曉 (喝, 貨, 忽) in XZ's Iranian practice, not 匣. Minorsky (comm. to §6.8) notes that De Goeje's Parghar for a rustāq S of the river in Ibn Rusta misled Marquart and Barthold, and that the Ḥudūd 'very rightly places Pirghar to the north of the river'. So the name points to the N bank, against juan 1, which lists 鉢利曷 among the countries reached by crossing the Oxus southward from Kumedh: IDENTIFICATION SHOULD BE RECONSIDERED (either XZ's Parghar is the N-bank Parkhar and the juan 1 grouping is loose, or a S-bank homonym is meant). Three syllables, Iranian; chance is moderate.

key_fit: 鉢=pa(t) MISMATCH for b (幫 p-, voiceless; key p 59/61, b/bh is 並: 跋/婆/縛, and non-Indic b is 縛 or 捕); 鐸=da(k) ok (定 d + -k, the -k renders the k of kṣ); 創=kṣa(ṅ) ok (初 tʂʰ- = kṣ as 叉/差/刹/芻; -ŋ before n echoes); 那=na ok

note: Everything but the initial fits Badaxšān: -dak-kṣa- is the key's closed-C1 pattern (鐸 -k + 初 kṣ), 創 -ŋ before 那 is an echo. So two Chinese transcriptions heard p-: *Padaxšān, presumably the local pronunciation in the 7th c. (Ji also reports Uchida's Padiyan for 拔底延). The identification is not affected.

Strong three-character fit with an attested form in the right place.

key_fit: 屈=ku ok (居勿反 = 見 k; key ku, kuk); 浪=ra(ṅ)/la(ṅ) ok (來 + -ŋ; the nasal coda echoes the following nasal onset); 拏=ṇa ok (孃, ṇ 7/7): -nn- NOT supported (key §4: 浪拏 is a single n/ṇ)

quote: entspricht dem Kut-lang-na (*Kurāna)*) des Hian-čuang.
site_lead: Kuran/Karan, upper Kokcha with the lapis-lazuli mines (Wood; Ḥudūd comm.: 'The Kuran tributary joins this river from the left, upstream from Yumgan')
note: The current *kuranna doubles the n, which the key's echo-coda rule rejects (key_notes §4 names this very target). Kurān with a single nasal fits; 拏 is retroflex, so XZ heard or Indianised -āṇa. The Xin Tangshu variants 倶蘭/倶爛那 also give kuran(a).

key_fit: 昏=xun/khun ok for Iranian x (曉 x-, 魂 rhyme -uən: rounded vowel; Indic kh would be 佉 溪; Iranian x is 曉: 喝, 貨, 忽); 馱=dā ok (定 d/dh); 多=t/dh final ok (non-Indic final consonant written with a full syllable, cf. 拘謎陀 Kumēdh, 弭秣賀 Maymurgh)

site_lead: Khandūd, Wakhan, S (Afghan) bank of the Panj (Ḥudūd comm.: 'Khamdadh is undoubtedly Khandud, a considerable village in Vakhan'; Stein)
note: 昏 is the Iranian x- (曉) with a rounded vowel and a dental nasal coda before d (m assimilated: md > nd); 馱多 render -dādh with the final consonant spelled out. The 10th-c. form Khamdādh with its Buddhist temples matches both the characters and XZ's 伽藍; better than the unattested *khandata (kh/Indic, final -a).

note: The early Arabic form Shikinān/Shiqinān (k/q, not the later γ of Šuγnān) fits 尸棄尼 = ši-khi-ni; 棄 (溪 kʰ) for Arabic q is the expected choice. Marquart reports Wukong's 赤匿/式匿 and the Tang 識匿/瑟匿 (Sik-ni).

current_form: *śami; 雙靡 (前漢書), 賒彌 (宋雲), 舎彌 (魏書)

Marquart (Ērānšahr 243-245) equates it with Song Yun's 賒彌 (old reading Śa-mi) and the Han 雙靡; Ji adds the Candragarbha's 賒摩. No attested Indic or Iranian form found: library searched for śāmi/śyāmi/śami + deśa/rāṣṭra/viṣaya/nagara (no country name). The country stays Chitral-Mastuj on other grounds.

key_fit: 波=pa ok (幫); 謎=mē (明 + 齊 e; as 拘謎陀 Kumēdh): e, not i; 羅=ra ok (來; here the final -r spelled with a full syllable, as non-Indic finals)

The Sanskrit form fits every character, including ś for 舍 (書); Mizutani's Prakritised *pu(m)ñasala breaks the sibilant (s = 心) and the echo-coda rule (no -mñ-). Ji also reads puṇyaśālā. key_fit: 烏=u/o ok (影 + 模: u ×2, o ×1); 鎩=ṣa/ṣai/ṣar (生 ṣ/š; three readings: 所例 祭 -ai, 所拜 皆 -ai, 所八 山入 -t: the -t reading gives ṣar as -t = r in XZ's Iranian practice)

But Uighur translators transcribed the Chinese, and NW Chinese -t > -r, so ušar is not independent evidence. No Iranian or Khotanese place name of this shape found in the Ḥudūd (Yarkand, Kashghar only) or Serindia. The name does not decide between Yarkand and Yangi Hissar.

current_form: Skt. khāsa; 室利訖栗多底 *śrī-kritati; old 疏勒
key_fit: 佉=kha ok (溪 kʰ-; key kha, khā); 沙=ṣa (生 ṣ: s would be 娑/薩 心) → khāsa MISMATCH on the sibilant. 室利訖栗多底: 室=ś before r ok; 利=rī ok; 訖=k (closed before r) ok; 栗=ṛ/ri ok; 多=ta ok; 底=ti ok → *śrīkṛtatī

attestation: Ji: 竭石/竭叉/佉沙 from *Khaṣa, the name of the Himalayan Khaśa people; Uighur Käš (Life), Kāšγar (Kāšγarī); Skt. khaṣa (var. of khaśa) as a people in the Mahābhārata tribute list (Sabhāparvan 2.48.20*475)

note: The sibilant is ṣ (生 13/13 in the key), which is also what XZ writes for Iranian š (鑊沙 Wakhsh). So the local name Kaš (Kāš-γar, Uighur Käš, with Saka -γar 'land', Pelliot via Ji) or a Sanskritised Khaṣa, not khāsa. Library: khaṣāḥ in MBh 2 App. (dākṣiṇātyāḥ pulindāś ca śambarāḥ kaṅkaṇāḥ khaṣāḥ, 2_epic/mbh/vyasa_mahabharata_parvan-02-sabhaparvan.txt:7735), but the Khaśa are a Himalayan people, so this only shows the Sanskrit spelling. The 'correct' name 室利訖栗多底 fits *śrīkṛtatī by the key (室利 = śrī as in the key's 室利-names); no attestation found (library: srikrt only in śrīkṛta compounds); Ji: 'the rest unknown'. Two characters for 佉沙: chance matches easy.

site_lead: Lop: Charkhlik (Nob-ched/'Great Nob') and Miran ('Little Nob') (Stein, Serindia 322)
note: Kingsmill's *navapura is excluded by the characters (only -pa). Mizutani's *navapa fits but has no meaning (Stein: it 'may look like Sanskrit, but certainly has no meaning'). Ji's *Navāp with a final -p fits as well and links to the attested Tib. Nob and Lop (Yule, Stein); the Sogdian etymology na'w + āp is Ji's and is not quoted from a Sogdian source here (reported, not in files). Both remain unattested as such; *Navāp is preferred only because it connects to Nob.
